Standard exercism beer-song. Implement Verse, Verses, Song.

Verse(n):
- if n < 0 or n > 99, error.
- verse 0: "No more bottles of beer on the wall, no more bottles of beer.\nGo to the store and buy some more, 99 bottles of beer on the wall.\n"
- verse 1: "1 bottle of beer on the wall, 1 bottle of beer.\nTake it down and pass it around, no more bottles of beer on the wall.\n"
- verse n: "{n} bottles of beer on the wall, {n} bottles of beer.\nTake one down and pass it around, {n-1} bottles of beer on the wall.\n" — but if n-1 == 1, then "1 bottle".

Verses(start, stop): error if start > stop, or if start > 99, or stop < 0. Concatenate Verse(i) for i from start down to stop.

Song() = Verses(99, 0).

Helper: bottles(n) returns "no more bottles", "1 bottle", "{n} bottles".

## Summary

Implemented the three functions in `beer_song.go` (leaving `beer_song_test.go` untouched):

- **`Verse(n)`** — returns the verse for `n` bottles, or an error if `n` is outside 0–99. It builds the verse from a shared `bottles(n)` helper that handles the special cases (`"no more bottles"`, `"1 bottle"`, `"{n} bottles"`), capitalizes the first line, and switches `"Take one down"` to `"Take it down"` for verse 1. Verse 0 is the "Go to the store" verse.
- **`Verses(start, stop)`** — validates the range (`start >= stop`, both in bounds) and concatenates verses from `start` down to `stop`, separated by blank lines.
- **`Song()`** — delegates to `Verses(99, 0)`.

Test results: `TestBottlesVerse`, `TestSeveralVerses`, and `TestEntireSong` all pass.
